subject: A transient network error is reported as a content regression by the lab smoke
description: Measured 2026-09-19 during the join-code deploy. _tools/smoke-lab-content-leaks.js documents its own contract: exit 1 = assertion failure (regression detected), exit 2 = infrastructure failure (puppeteer launch, network, missing deps). A net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED blip on bc1-cf mid-run instead produced ASSERTION failures - 'load - EXCEPTION: CONFIG-GLOBAL PISL09Config never attached, and 7 request(s) FAILED: net::ERR_NETWORK_CHANGED' and 'no js errors - console.error: Failed to load resource' - so it reported 8 PASS / 2 FAIL, post-verify flagged a divergence, and the Confluence regen was SKIPPED. An immediate re-run was 10/0 exit 0, proving it transient and not a regression from the deploy (which touched only console.html, a file pis-l09 does not load). The defect: a network failure is indistinguishable from a content regression in the output, which is the detector-keyed-on-the-wrong-surface shape - and the cost is that a real regression and a blip look identical, so the next person learns to shrug at this gate. Fix: when a request failure with a net:: error code is present, classify as infrastructure (exit 2) and say so, rather than letting the downstream assertions fail as if the bytes were wrong. The script already has the exit code for it.
